IMPLEMENTED — Gerrit change 1179 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1179), commit
30ab72cc10 on branch jira-family-seam, based on origin/main 96b82de1e0.

=== AC-BY-AC EVIDENCE ===

[AC1] `retry.py` exists with all six members; `transport.py` no longer defines them.
New file `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/retry.py` defines
`_connection_retry_exceptions`, `_jira_http_error_types`, `_as_backend_http_error`,
`TlsVerificationError`, `_tls_verification_error`, `_with_connection_retry`. All six `def`/`class`
statements are deleted from `transport.py` (it now only IMPORTS them).

[AC2] `TlsVerificationError` lives in `retry.py` with its factory; NO circular import.
Both are in `retry.py`. Verified by importing in BOTH orders in a clean interpreter — `retry` then
`transport`, and `transport` then `retry` — each succeeds. Also asserted object identity across the
re-export, which is the stronger check: `transport.TlsVerificationError is retry.TlsVerificationError`
-> True, and `transport._with_connection_retry is retry._with_connection_retry` -> True. So a caller
reaching through `transport` gets the SAME object, not a copy that could drift.

[AC3] Re-export works and `test_jira_dc_config_settings.py` passes with ZERO edits.
`git diff --exit-code` on that file returns clean (exit 0), and the file passes 11/11. In fact
`git diff --stat tests/` is EMPTY for the whole change — no test file is touched at all.

[AC4] The full DC transport unit suite passes with zero test edits.
**79 passed** across test_dc_pat_required_heldout.py, test_dc_transport_pagination_heldout.py,
test_identity_dc_inbound_heldout.py, test_jira_datacenter_backend_port.py,
test_jira_dc_config_settings.py, test_jira_dc_harness_shape.py, test_jira_dc_transport_heldout.py,
test_jira_dc_transport.py. No test needed an edit, so the relocation is behaviour-preserving by the
plan's own criterion.

[AC5] Under the cap, with headroom for S2. MEASURED BEFORE/AFTER, as this AC requires:
  transport.py  789 -> 683 lines  (106 removed; 117 lines of headroom under the 800 cap)
  retry.py        0 -> 162 lines  (new; above the 100-LOC floor the module-size policy sets)
The repo-wide module-size gate reports NO file over the cap.

[AC6] A reviewer can confirm it is a move by reading the diff.
Stronger than that, and measured rather than asserted: the 132 relocated lines are BYTE-IDENTICAL to
the deleted ones. Verified by extracting lines 137-268 from `git show HEAD~1:...transport.py` and
diffing against `retry.py` minus its new 30-line header — `diff` reports no difference. No control
flow, retry count (3 attempts), backoff value ((2, 5) seconds), or exception type changed.

=== ONE DELIBERATE ADDITION BEYOND A BARE MOVE, AND WHY ===
Ruff (F401) fails a bare re-export: five of the six names are unused WITHIN `transport.py`
(`_with_connection_retry` is the exception — 17 call sites). Rather than scatter `# noqa`, the change
adds an `__all__` facade with a comment, which is the idiom the SIBLING Cloud adapter already adopted
for exactly this situation after its own J2 relocation (`adapters/jira/acli.py:84-86`: "keeps
resolving for callers and the characterization suites; ``__all__`` records them as intentional
re-exports"). Following the established local precedent rather than inventing a second convention.

=== GATES ===
`make lint` PASSED (ruff check + format-check, zizmor, actionlint). `make typecheck` PASSED — mypy
clean over 405 source files. Awaiting Gerrit LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.

# S1 — extract the retry/error cluster out of `transport.py` (behaviour-preserving)

## Context / Problem

Split out of [rebar:b586-2fda-8a15-4260], whose plan hit BLOCK ten times. The round-by-round
record is on that ticket; the structural finding is that it carried TWO independent changes — a
mechanical relocation and a new 429 policy — and every round found new surface because a fix to
one re-opened the other. Rounds 6-7 were about THIS half's mechanics; rounds 1, 4, 8, 9, 10 were
about the policy half (now S2). Splitting is the same move that turned J9's eight BLOCKs into a
first-try PASS as J10.

This story is the mechanical half and is **forced by the module-size cap, not by taste**:
`transport.py` is **789 lines on `origin/main`** against the LOCKED 800-line cap
(`.github/module-size-limit.txt`), so there are ELEVEN lines of headroom and the 429 policy cannot
be added in place. (Recording the measurement because this file's LOC has been misquoted twice in
epic e369: the earlier "792 vs 789" disagreement was a pre-/post-9263 base difference, and now
that 9263 is merged both readings agree at 789.)

## Approach

**Relocate, do not redesign.** Move the retry/error cluster from
`adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py` into a new `adapters/jira_datacenter/retry.py`, changing
no behaviour. The cluster is `_connection_retry_exceptions`, `_jira_http_error_types`,
`_as_backend_http_error`, `TlsVerificationError`, `_tls_verification_error`, and
`_with_connection_retry`.

**`TlsVerificationError` MUST move with the rest.** `_tls_verification_error` returns it, so
leaving the class behind in `transport.py` makes `retry.py` import from `transport.py` while
`transport.py` imports `_with_connection_retry` from `retry.py` — a circular import. The class and
its factory are one unit.

**Re-export from `transport.py` so existing importers keep working.** `test_jira_dc_config_settings.py`
imports `TlsVerificationError` from the transport module; that test must pass UNEDITED, because
editing it to chase the move would convert a regression signal into a rubber stamp.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/retry.py` — NEW; the moved cluster.
- `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py` — cluster deleted,
  cluster imported, names re-exported.

**NOT in scope:** any behaviour change, and specifically any 429 / `Retry-After` handling — that is
S2. If this story changes what any call does, it has failed.

## Testing

The oracle for a pure relocation is that the EXISTING suite passes unedited — a new test asserting
the code moved would only restate the diff.

* `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` DC transport tests pass with NO edits.
* `test_jira_dc_config_settings.py` passes with NO edits (proves the re-export works).
* The module-size gate passes, and `transport.py` is measurably smaller.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `retry.py` exists and contains all six named members, and `transport.py` no longer defines
      them
- [ ] `TlsVerificationError` lives in `retry.py` WITH `_tls_verification_error`, and a test or a
      clean `python -c "import ..."` proves there is no circular import between the two modules
- [ ] `transport.py` re-exports the moved names, and `test_jira_dc_config_settings.py` passes
      **with zero edits to that file** — asserted by `git diff --exit-code` on it
- [ ] the full DC transport unit suite passes with zero test edits; if any test needed an edit,
      this story is not behaviour-preserving and must be reworked rather than the test adjusted
- [ ] `transport.py` is under the 800-line cap with headroom for S2, and the measured before/after
      line counts are recorded on this ticket
- [ ] NO diff hunk changes control flow, retry counts, backoff values, or exception types — a
      reviewer can confirm the change is a move by reading the diff alone
